claim: The teleost medaka (Oryzias latipes) grows roughly ten-fold from hatching to sexual maturity within 2–3 months.
source: The teleost medaka (Oryzias latipes) grows roughly ten-fold from hatching to sexual maturity within 2–3 months (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A which shows photos of newly hatched and young sexually mature adult medaka with highlighted eye areas.

claim: Highly visual shallow water fish such as medaka have near-perfect hemispherical eyes.
source: Highly visual shallow water fish such as medaka have near-perfect hemispherical eyes (Fernald, 1990; Nishiwaki et al., 1997; Beck et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies.

claim: The vertebrate eye consists of multiple concentric tissues, including the neural retina (NR) and the retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE).
source: The vertebrate eye consists of multiple concentric tissues, including the neural retina (NR) and the retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE) (Figure 1A; Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A showing schematic anatomy of the fish eye and Table 1 listing abbreviations.

claim: In fish and amphibians, the neural retina and retinal pigmented epithelium grow from a ring-shaped stem cell niche in the retinal periphery called the ciliary marginal zone (CMZ).
source: In fish and amphibians, these tissues grow from a ring-shaped stem cell niche in the retinal periphery: the ciliary marginal zone (CMZ) (Johns, 1977; Harris and Perron, 1998; Amato et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies.

claim: The CMZ can be subdivided into a peripheral stem- and a central progenitor cell domain.
source: The CMZ can be subdivided into a peripheral stem- and a central progenitor cell domain; stem cells are believed to have the potential for indefinitely many cell divisions while progenitor cells divide only a handful of times (Raymond et al., 2006; Centanin et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2016; Shi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to four published studies.

claim: At the very periphery of the CMZ, about 5 rows of cells express the stem cell marker retina-specific homeobox gene 2 (Rx2).
source: At the very periphery of the CMZ, about 5 rows of cells express the stem cell marker retina-specific homeobox gene 2 (Rx2) (Reinhardt et al., 2015; Wan et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies.

claim: The CMZ is a bi-partite niche, with tissue-specific stem cells for NR and RPE.
source: The CMZ is a bi-partite niche, with tissue-specific stem cells for NR and RPE (Shi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: In medaka, stem cells for NR and RPE are strictly separate, as demonstrated by transplantations at blastula stage and genetic recombination after hatching.
source: In medaka, stem cells for NR and RPE are strictly separate, as demonstrated by transplantations at blastula stage and genetic recombination after hatching (Centanin et al., 2011; Centanin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: CMZ cells appositionally add new cells in concentric rings as shown by label incorporation with thymidine analogues.
source: As a population, CMZ cells appositionally add new cells in concentric rings as shown by label incorporation with thymidine analogues (Johns, 1977; Centanin et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: Individual stem cells labelled by genetic markers form clonal progeny in so-called Arched Continuous Stripes (ArCoS).
source: Individual stem cells labelled by genetic markers form clonal progeny in so-called Arched Continuous Stripes (ArCoS; Figure 1B) (Centanin et al., 2011; Centanin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies and reference to Figure 1B showing growth patterns.

claim: Medaka NR stem cells produce the full complement of neuronal cells in apico-basal clonal columns.
source: Medaka NR stem cells produce the full complement of neuronal cells in apico-basal clonal columns (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A'–B) (Centanin et al., 2011; Centanin et al., 2014; Lust and Wittbrodt, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2A'–B.

claim: Differentiated retinal cells grow little in size.
source: These differentiated retinal cells grow little in size (Johns, 1977), retain their relative position over time (Johns, 1977; Centanin et al., 2011), and have negligible death rates (Johns and Easter, 1977; Stenkamp, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Differentiated retinal cells retain their relative position over time.
source: These differentiated retinal cells grow little in size (Johns, 1977), retain their relative position over time (Johns, 1977; Centanin et al., 2011), and have negligible death rates (Johns and Easter, 1977; Stenkamp, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: Differentiated retinal cells have negligible death rates.
source: These differentiated retinal cells grow little in size (Johns, 1977), retain their relative position over time (Johns, 1977; Centanin et al., 2011), and have negligible death rates (Johns and Easter, 1977; Stenkamp, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: The only parameter available to NR and RPE to coordinate their growth rates is the proliferation of the tissue-specific CMZ stem cells.
source: Thus, the only parameter available to NR and RPE to coordinate their growth rates is the proliferation of the tissue-specific CMZ stem cells.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the preceding statements about differentiated retinal cells having little growth, fixed positions, and negligible death rates.

claim: The medaka retina diverges from the neutral drift model.
source: Strikingly, the medaka retina diverges from the neutral drift model.
evidence: The claim is supported by the subsequent statements about the CMZ maintaining a polyclonal stem cell population and NR stem cells undergoing asymmetric self-renewing divisions.

claim: The CMZ maintains a polyclonal stem cell population for both the NR and the RPE.
source: The CMZ maintains a polyclonal stem cell population for both the NR and the RPE, and in particular NR stem cells undergo asymmetric self-renewing divisions throughout the life of the animal (Centanin et al., 2011; Centanin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: NR stem cells undergo asymmetric self-renewing divisions throughout the life of the animal.
source: The CMZ maintains a polyclonal stem cell population for both the NR and the RPE, and in particular NR stem cells undergo asymmetric self-renewing divisions throughout the life of the animal (Centanin et al., 2011; Centanin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: RPE stem cells have highly variable cell division timing consistent with a downstream role in the control hierarchy.
source: We find that RPE stem cells have highly variable cell division timing consistent with a downstream role in the control hierarchy, whereas NR stem cells display less variability consistent with an upstream role in inducing growth in nearby tissues.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and simulations presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figure 3.

claim: NR stem cells display less variability in cell division timing consistent with an upstream role in inducing growth in nearby tissues.
source: We find that RPE stem cells have highly variable cell division timing consistent with a downstream role in the control hierarchy, whereas NR stem cells display less variability consistent with an upstream role in inducing growth in nearby tissues.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and simulations presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figure 3.

claim: The spatial segregation of stem and progenitor CMZ domains is an emergent property of the system.
source: Our simulation predicts that the spatial segregation of stem and progenitor CMZ domains is an emergent property, as the topology of the retinal niche preconditions the retina to a spatially biased neutral drift.
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results presented in Figure 4.

claim: The topology of the retinal niche preconditions the retina to a spatially biased neutral drift.
source: Our simulation predicts that the spatial segregation of stem and progenitor CMZ domains is an emergent property, as the topology of the retinal niche preconditions the retina to a spatially biased neutral drift.
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results presented in Figure 4.

claim: NR stem cells deviate from a purely random drift model by preferential division axis orientation.
source: NR stem cells deviate from a purely random drift model by preferential division axis orientation and differential modulation of division parameters along the CMZ circumference.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and simulations presented in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: NR stem cells deviate from a purely random drift model by differential modulation of division parameters along the CMZ circumference.
source: NR stem cells deviate from a purely random drift model by preferential division axis orientation and differential modulation of division parameters along the CMZ circumference.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and simulations presented in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: During post-embryonic growth of the teleost eye, the NR CMZ forms a hub for integrating external and internal stimuli that affect cell division parameters.
source: We propose that during post-embryonic growth of the teleost eye, the NR CMZ forms a hub for integrating external and internal stimuli that affect cell division parameters, which ultimately direct the growth and shape of the entire eye.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on the findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cell division parameters in the NR CMZ ultimately direct the growth and shape of the entire eye.
source: We propose that during post-embryonic growth of the teleost eye, the NR CMZ forms a hub for integrating external and internal stimuli that affect cell division parameters, which ultimately direct the growth and shape of the entire eye.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on the findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: RPE ArCoS frequently branched, forming irregular stripes variable in size and shape.
source: RPE ArCoS frequently branched, forming irregular stripes variable in size and shape (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1E showing proximal view of unpigmented lineages in the RPE.

claim: NR patches formed a narrow stripe, while the width of RPE patches showed much greater variation.
source: Confirming our previous qualitative observations, NR patches formed a narrow stripe, while the width of RPE patches showed much greater variation (Figure 3C'; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 3C' and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A showing patch superposition and width distributions.

claim: The variance of NR and RPE patches was significantly different at the 0.05 level (p=3.50∙10−12, F-test of equality of variance).
source: The variance of NR and RPE patches was significantly different at the 0.05 level (p=3.50∙10−12, F-test of equality of variance).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Simulated patches in the inducer growth mode had low variation in width, while patches in the responder growth mode spread widely.
source: In striking agreement to the experimental data, simulated patches in the inducer growth mode had low variation in width, while patches in the responder growth mode spread widely (Figure 3C''; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 3C'' and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A showing simulated patch superposition and width distributions.

claim: The variances in the simulated conditions were significantly different at the 0.05 level (p=5.84∙10−7, F-test of equality of variance).
source: The variances in the simulated conditions were significantly different at the 0.05 level (p=5.84∙10−7, F-test of equality of variance), but highly similar between NR and inducer (p=0.56, F-test of equality of variance); and RPE and responder (p=0.21, F-test of equality of variance).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of the simulated data.

claim: Patches in the NR and in the inducer growth mode were overwhelmingly stripe-like with no branch points.
source: Patches in the NR and in the inducer growth mode were overwhelmingly stripe-like with no branch points (Figure 3D; inset I), with similar node distribution (p=0.64, Wilcoxon rank sum test).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 3D showing distribution of number of nodes and statistical analysis.

claim: Both NR and inducer differed significantly at the 0.05 level from the distribution in the RPE and responder growth mode (NR-RPE: p=3.93∙10−6; NR-responder: p=3.26∙10−4; inducer-RPE: p=6.24∙10−7; inducer-responder: p=7.00∙10−5, Wilcoxon rank sum test).
source: In contrast, both NR and inducer differed significantly at the 0.05 level from the distribution in the RPE and responder growth mode (NR-RPE: p=3.93∙10−6; NR-responder: p=3.26∙10−4; inducer-RPE: p=6.24∙10−7; inducer-responder: p=7.00∙10−5, Wilcoxon rank sum test).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of the experimental and simulated data.

claim: Patches in the RPE and in the responder growth mode frequently bifurcated or merged, creating branching shapes with inclusions indicative of clone intermingling.
source: Patches in the RPE and in the responder growth mode frequently bifurcated or merged, creating branching shapes with inclusions indicative of clone intermingling (Figure 3D; inset III).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 3D showing distribution of number of nodes.

claim: In the NR late patches clustered in the central post-embryonic retina and waned thereafter.
source: In the NR late patches clustered in the central post-embryonic retina and waned thereafter.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data presented in Figure 3E showing rug plot of late arising patches.

claim: The RPE displayed an even distribution of late patches indicative of frequent fragmentation throughout the life of the animal (NR-RPE: p=1.74∙10−3, Wilcoxon rank sum test).
source: In contrast, the RPE displayed an even distribution indicative of frequent fragmentation throughout the life of the animal as predicted for the highly variable scenario (NR-RPE: p=1.74∙10−3, Wilcoxon rank sum test).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data presented in Figure 3E and statistical analysis.

claim: NR and RPE have different degrees of variability in cell division timing.
source: Together, these data show that NR and RPE have different degrees of variability in cell division timing.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The NR displayed lower variability consistent with the simulated inducer growth mode.
source: The NR displayed lower variability consistent with the simulated inducer growth mode, while the RPE showed higher levels of variability that even exceeded what we modelled with the responder growth mode.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The RPE showed higher levels of variability that even exceeded what was modelled with the responder growth mode.
source: The NR displayed lower variability consistent with the simulated inducer growth mode, while the RPE showed higher levels of variability that even exceeded what we modelled with the responder growth mode.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The virtual induction ring contained many few-cell clones unrelated to any ArCoS.
source: Surprisingly, the virtual induction ring contained many few-cell clones unrelated to any ArCoS (Figure 4A', encircled by pink dashed lines).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 4A' showing detail of inducer growth mode simulation.

claim: In terminated clones, all stem cells left the niche and thus differentiated.
source: In these clones, all stem cells left the niche and thus differentiated ('terminated clones').
evidence: The claim is a definition based on the simulation results.

claim: The overwhelming majority of virtual ArCoS emerged from the periphery of the induction ring.
source: Notably, the overwhelming majority of virtual ArCoS emerged from the periphery of the induction ring (Figure 4A'–A''; Video 4), as confirmed by tracing back the position of the founder stem cells at simulation step 0, while centrally located cells formed exclusively terminated clones (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 4A'–A'', Video 4, and Figure 4B showing simulation results.

claim: Centrally located cells formed exclusively terminated clones.
source: Notably, the overwhelming majority of virtual ArCoS emerged from the periphery of the induction ring (Figure 4A'–A''; Video 4), as confirmed by tracing back the position of the founder stem cells at simulation step 0, while centrally located cells formed exclusively terminated clones (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 4B showing simulation results.

claim: Only a minority of virtual stem cells formed ArCoS, while the vast majority formed terminated clones.
source: Strikingly, only a minority of virtual stem cells formed ArCoS, while the vast majority formed terminated clones (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 4B showing simulation results.

claim: The virtual stem cell population subdivided into two functional domains that mirror the current model of the retinal niche with a peripheral stem- and a central progenitor domain.
source: Together, these data show that the virtual stem cell population subdivided into two functional domains that mirror the current model of the retinal niche with a peripheral stem- and a central progenitor domain (Raymond et al., 2006; Shi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the simulation results and is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: This subdivision was not imposed onto the simulation, but emerged dynamically.
source: Importantly, this subdivision was not imposed onto the simulation, but emerged dynamically.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the simulation results.

claim: The central-most cells were poised to differentiate by being pushed out of the niche by divisions of their more peripheral neighbors.
source: The central-most cells were poised to differentiate by being pushed out of the niche by divisions of their more peripheral neighbors.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the simulation results.

claim: Few-cell clusters in the induction ring vastly outnumbered ArCoS, showing that terminated clones were the most common type of clone (n = 1129 terminated clones in 20 retinae).
source: Few-cell clusters in the induction ring vastly outnumbered ArCoS, showing that terminated clones were the most common type of clone (n = 1129 terminated clones in 20 retinae; Figure 4C'–C'', Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 4C'–C'' and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: ArCoS were less frequent (n = 36 ArCoS in 20 retinae).
source: ArCoS, which by definition always reach the retinal margin, were less frequent (Figure 4C'–C'', pink arrowheads; n = 36 ArCoS in 20 retinae).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 4C'–C''.

claim: Rx2-expressing cells in the CMZ included cells that proliferated indefinitely as well as cells that proliferated only a few times before differentiating.
source: Thus, Rx2-expressing cells in the CMZ included cells that proliferated indefinitely as well as cells that proliferated only a few times before differentiating.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data showing both ArCoS and terminated clones.

claim: Among terminated clones, the majority started in central positions (experiment: 77.3%; simulation: 61.0%).
source: Among terminated clones, the majority started in central positions (experiment: 77.3%; simulation: 61.0%), while a minority were exclusively located in the peripheral induction ring or in the post-embryonic retina (experiment: 22.7%; simulation: 39.0%).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental and simulated data presented in Figure 4F.

claim: Among experimental ArCoS, the vast majority (86.1%) started in the periphery, but 13.9% derived from a central position.
source: Among experimental ArCoS, the vast majority (86.1%) started in the periphery, but 13.9% derived from a central position, showing that some cells located in the central progenitor domain of the CMZ drifted into a lifelong stem cell fate.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4F.

claim: The ratios for peripheral and central ArCoS in the simulation are nearly identical to experimental data (p=1.00, 2-sample test for equality of proportions).
source: Strikingly, the ratios for peripheral and central ArCoS in the simulation are nearly identical (p=1.00, 2-sample test for equality of proportions), showing that the simulation captures ArCoS dynamics extremely well.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis comparing experimental and simulated data.

claim: NR ArCoS formed stripes that appeared slightly narrower than in the simulation.
source: NR ArCoS formed stripes that appeared slightly narrower than in the simulation (Figure 3A'–A'', C'–C'').
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 3A'–A'' and C'–C'' showing experimental and simulated data.

claim: In simulations, the division axis was not oriented ('random division axis').
source: In simulations, the division axis was not oriented ('random division axis').
evidence: The claim describes a parameter of the simulation model.

claim: The thin clonal stripes suggested that NR stem cells had a preferential axis of division along the radial (central-peripheral) coordinate.
source: The thin clonal stripes suggested that NR stem cells had a preferential axis of division along the radial (central-peripheral) coordinate, while circumferential divisions occurred with lower frequency than expected for a random division axis orientation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observed clonal stripe patterns.

claim: Experimental ArCoS width averaged to 4.87° (n = 99 ArCoS across seven retinae).
source: Experimental ArCoS width averaged to 4.87° (Figure 5D' black graph; n = 99 ArCoS across seven retinae).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 5D'.

claim: ArCoS width in simulations with random division axis averaged to 7.28° (n = 102 clones from five simulation runs; compared to experimental data: p=1.94∙10−7, Welch two-sample t-test).
source: In contrast to experimental data, ArCoS width in simulations with random division axis averaged to 7.28° (Figure 5D' blue graph; n = 102 clones from five simulation runs; compared to experimental data: p=1.94∙10−7, Welch two-sample t-test).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulated data, reference to Figure 5D', and statistical analysis.

claim: In simulations with ideal division axis, ArCoS width closely matched experimental data, averaging at 4.54° (n = 133 clones from five simulation runs; compared to experimental data: p=0.37, Welch two-sample t-test).
source: In simulations with ideal division axis, ArCoS width closely matched experimental data, averaging at 4.54° (Figure 5D', red graph; n = 133 clones from five simulation runs; compared to experimental data: p=0.37, Welch two-sample t-test).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulated data, reference to Figure 5D', and statistical analysis.

claim: NR stem cell divisions were not randomly oriented, but instead were preferentially oriented along the central-peripheral axis.
source: These data show that NR stem cell divisions were not randomly oriented, but instead were preferentially oriented along the central-peripheral axis.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data presented in Figure 5.

claim: NR stem cells underwent radial and circumferential divisions at a rate consistent with a role in organ shape regulation.
source: Moreover NR stem cells underwent radial and circumferential divisions at a rate consistent with a role in organ shape regulation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data presented in Figure 5.

claim: In the retina of the surface-dwelling medaka, the position of the embryonic retina was not centered, but instead was shifted ventrally.
source: We observed that in the retina of the surface-dwelling medaka, the position of the embryonic retina was not centered, but instead was shifted ventrally (Figure 6A').
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 6A' showing proximal view of NR clones.

claim: The post-embryonic retina was longer dorsally than ventrally (ratio dorsal to ventral length: mean = 1.42; standard deviation = 0.29; n = 10 retinae).
source: As a result, the post-embryonic retina was longer dorsally than ventrally (ratio dorsal to ventral length: mean = 1.42; standard deviation = 0.29; n = 10 retinae).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The ventral-ward shift indicated that along the CMZ circumference, ventral stem cells had different division parameters.
source: The ventral-ward shift indicated that along the CMZ circumference, ventral stem cells had different division parameters.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observed ventral shift of the embryonic retina.

claim: Ventral NR stem cells have a different behavior than elsewhere along the circumference, leading to a ventral-ward shift of the embryonic retina.
source: In conclusion, ventral NR stem cells have a different behavior than elsewhere along the circumference, leading to a ventral-ward shift of the embryonic retina.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data presented in Figure 6.

claim: The simulations suggest that the different behavior of ventral NR stem cells consists of modulation of proliferation parameters by an extrinsic signal in the ventral CMZ.
source: The simulations suggest that this different behavior consists of modulation of proliferation parameters by an extrinsic signal in the ventral CMZ.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the simulated data presented in Figure 6.

claim: Eye size in fish scales to the body size.
source: Eye size in fish scales to the body size (Lyall, 1957; Johns and Easter, 1977).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: Body size, and thus eye growth rates greatly vary among individuals and depend on environmental factors.
source: Body size, and thus eye growth rates greatly vary among individuals and depend on environmental factors (Johns, 1981).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: RPE cells divided with high variability, indicative of periods of long quiescence where they waited for proliferative cues.
source: RPE cells divided with high variability, indicative of periods of long quiescence where they waited for proliferative cues.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data.

claim: NR cells displayed lower variability, supporting an upstream role in regulating growth.
source: NR cells displayed lower variability, supporting an upstream role in regulating growth (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental and simulated data and is supported by reference to Figure 7A.

claim: Hair follicle cells in mouse induce the growth of underlying adipose tissue through hedgehog signalling.
source: Such division of labor among tissues might apply more generally to multiple organ systems, for example hair follicle cells in mouse induce the growth of underlying adipose tissue through hedgehog signalling (Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Hedgehog signalling regulates the NR/RPE boundary in the CMZ of medaka.
source: Intriguingly, hedgehog signalling also regulates the NR/RPE boundary in the CMZ of medaka (Reinhardt et al., 2015), suggesting that signals mediating coordination of proliferative cell populations might be conserved.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: All virtual cells had equal potency, yet only a fraction realized their full stem cell potential.
source: All virtual cells had equal potency, yet only a fraction realized their full stem cell potential.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the simulation results.

claim: Peripheral cells had a high chance to become canalized in a stem cell fate, while central cells were more likely to act as progenitor cells with limited proliferation potential.
source: Peripheral cells had a high chance to become canalized in a stem cell fate, while central cells were more likely to act as progenitor cells with limited proliferation potential (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the simulation results and is supported by reference to Figure 7B.

claim: Retrograde movement of row 2 cells into row 1 of the CMZ occurs in vivo.
source: Interestingly, retrograde movement of row 2 cells into row 1 of the CMZ occurs in vivo (Wan et al., 2016), which we also observed in our simulations.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study and observation in the simulations.

claim: All terminated clones examined were multipotent and spanned all retinal layers.
source: All terminated clones we examined were multipotent and spanned all retinal layers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Neutral drift in a finite-sized environment such as adult mammalian tissues must ultimately result in a monoclonal niche.
source: Neutral drift in a finite-sized environment such as adult mammalian tissues must ultimately result in a monoclonal niche (Snippert et al., 2010; Colom and Jones, 2016; Clevers and Watt, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies.

claim: In fish, homeostatic growth expands niches, and thus the number of stem cells increases.
source: In fish, homeostatic growth expands niches, and thus the number of stem cells increases (Centanin et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Neutral drift leads to gradual loss of polyclonality in the intestine and muscle of fish.
source: Indeed, neutral drift leads to gradual loss of polyclonality in the intestine and muscle of fish (Aghaallaei et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: In the intestine of both mammals and fish, physical isolation of multiple niches results in a polyclonal organ built up of monoclonal units.
source: In the intestine of both mammals and fish, physical isolation of multiple niches results in a polyclonal organ built up of monoclonal units (Snippert et al., 2010; Aghaallaei et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: The CMZ is a physically contiguous niche that nevertheless maintains polyclonality lifelong both in the NR and the RPE.
source: In contrast, the CMZ is a physically contiguous niche that nevertheless maintains polyclonality lifelong both in the NR and the RPE (Centanin et al., 2011; Centanin et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: For a radially expanding population, it has been mathematically proven that (assuming pure neutral genetic drift) no single clone will ever take over and clonal sectors perpetually coexist.
source: Specifically for a radially expanding population, it has been mathematically proven that (assuming pure neutral genetic drift) no single clone will ever take over and clonal sectors perpetually coexist (Hallatschek and Nelson, 2010; Korolev et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: Growth of the perimeter is faster than circumferential expansion of clones, thus preserving population diversity.
source: Growth of the perimeter is faster than circumferential expansion of clones, thus preserving population diversity (Hallatschek and Nelson, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: In the NR, the biased division axis further reduces competition, thus increasing niche polyclonality.
source: Interestingly, in the NR, the biased division axis further reduces competition (Figure 5), thus increasing niche polyclonality.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data presented in Figure 5.

claim: The geometry of the CMZ niche prohibits the total loss of polyclonality.
source: In summary, the geometry of the CMZ niche prohibits the total loss of polyclonality.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the preceding discussion.

claim: Across vertebrates, the retina integrates visual input to adapt organ shape to optimize optics, a process called 'emmetropization'.
source: Across vertebrates, the retina integrates visual input to adapt organ shape to optimize optics, a process called 'emmetropization' (Wallman and Winawer, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: In chicken, emmetropization is regulated by specialized neurons distributed across the retina that send their axons to the CMZ, implicating the CMZ in regulation of eye shape.
source: In chicken, emmetropization is regulated by specialized neurons distributed across the retina that send their axons to the CMZ, implicating the CMZ in regulation of eye shape (Fischer et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Visual cues guide emmetropization in fish.
source: Visual cues also guide emmetropization in fish (Kröger and Wagner, 1996; Shen et al., 2005; Shen and Sivak, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies.

claim: Eye growth in young fish predominantly occurs by cell addition.
source: Eye growth in young fish predominantly occurs by cell addition, while in older fish CMZ proliferation decreases (Johns, 1981) coincident with a decrease in emmetropization plasticity (Shen and Sivak, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: In older fish CMZ proliferation decreases coincident with a decrease in emmetropization plasticity.
source: Eye growth in young fish predominantly occurs by cell addition, while in older fish CMZ proliferation decreases (Johns, 1981) coincident with a decrease in emmetropization plasticity (Shen and Sivak, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: In fish, emmetropization correlates with CMZ proliferation.
source: Thus, in fish, emmetropization correlates with CMZ proliferation.
